notes: The page is a small low-resolution image; the placement of pieces in steps 2 and 3 is a best-effort reading.

Step 1: Plate Round 4x4 (b1). Step 2: Plate 2x4 (b2) placed on the round plate, with black clip plates attached to its underside at the right end. Step 3: more clip plates and a black claw on a clip at the right; the grey piece at the left of step 3 could not be identified and is omitted.
Clip plates sit below b2, so they have no pieces under them. Their join to b2 is recorded as an edge instead of rests_on.
b2's contact with b1 is recorded as a stud/anti-stud join (exact stud ports are approximate because the 2x4 overlaps a round plate).
Step 4: Brick Round 4x4 with centre hole (b8) placed on the round plate b1 and the 2x4 plate b2. Step 5: eye tile (b9) on b8, plus a black claw (b10) clipped to a clip plate at the lower right.
Rests_on for the pieces: b8 on [b1, b2]; b9 on [b8]; b10 on [] (clipped, not resting).

The claw placement in step 5 is a best guess. Step 4 shows no claw at the right, so the step 3 claw (b7) may have been misread. The curved black shape at the lower right could be two claws, but only one is added here.

Step 6: the callout piece is read as the black wing-end curved wedge (b11, lego-47458) placed on the round brick b8. A black 65° slope (b12) is also visible beside the eye tile. This is read as added in the same step.
Step 7: two orange pieces are read as Pearl Gold 3048c slopes (b13, b14), placed on the round brick b8 at the front-left and back-right.
Exact stud positions on b8 are approximate because of the low image resolution. rests_on is b8 for each piece, so the edges only record that.
Step 8 builds a wing twice (2x) and clips both to the sides of the model, which is also turned over. The copies are listed as separate pieces b15-b17 and b18-b20.

Each wing has a handle plate (60478) and a black clip plate (61252) on one stud. A light bluish gray curved brick (11477) sits over the other stud. I read the 'rests_on' of the clip plate and the curved brick as the handle plate (b15 or b18).
Which clips on the body the handles attach to is a guess. b5 and b6 are used because b3 and b4 already hold claws. The picture shows the wings on opposite sides.
The clip plate on each wing is recorded as hanging on the handle plate's underside. This is uncertain.
This page starts a new sub-assembly, shown in the preview box at the top. It is a separate build, not yet attached to the main model.

Step 1: 2x4 plate b21. Step 2: 2x3 light gray plate b22 on b21, offset so one end of b21 stays exposed. Step 3: two black 1x2 plates (b23, b24) added at the ends. Step 3 may be viewed from another angle, so their positions and the count of two are guesses.
Step 4: two 65° slopes (light bluish gray b25, black b26) on the 2x3 plate b22. Step 5: dark gray towball plate b27 on the front studs of b22. Step 6: a dark gray triple wedge slope b28 over it.
In step 6 a dark curved fin rises at the back. I couldn't identify it, so it is left out.
Exact stud ports are approximate because of the low resolution. Treat rests_on as: b25 and b26 on [b22]; b27 on [b22]; b28 on [b22, b27].
Step 7 looks like the model turned to show another side. I couldn't see a new piece there, so nothing is added.
Callout sub-assembly: a black inverted slope (b30, lego-3049d) goes on the studs of a towball plate (b29), and a Pearl Gold cheese slope (b31) goes on top.

Step 8: the callout sub-assembly clips onto the front towball b27 via the socket underside of b29. I picked 14419 (socket and ball) because the ball must be reached through a socket. This is an inference.
Pearl Gold is read from the orange colour in the image.
rests_on: b29 clutches nothing underneath (hung by ball/socket), b30 on [b29], b31 on [b30].
Step 9 adds no new pieces. The leg sub-assembly (b29-b31 and b21-b28) is joined to the underside of the body.
I couldn't see the exact join point from the image. I recorded it as the leg's free stud on b30 going into the underside of the round plate b1. This is a guess.
I also assume the leg sub-assembly is already one piece through the ball join on b27/b29.

This page starts the second leg sub-assembly. Steps 1-3 repeat page 6 exactly, so the pieces are interpreted the same way: b32 is the 2x4 plate, b33 the 2x3 light gray plate, and b34 and b35 the two black 1x2 plates.
The preview box shows the finished leg. It looks like a mirrored version of the first leg, with orange pieces on top.
The second leg is the mirror of the first. Step 4 puts the black slope (b36) on the left and the light bluish gray slope (b37) on the right, the reverse of the first leg.
Step 5 adds the towball plate (b38) at the front. Step 6 adds the dark triple wedge (b39).
As on page 7, a dark fin shape at the back in step 6 could not be identified and is left out. Stud ports are approximate. Treat rests_on as: b36 and b37 on [b33]; b38 on [b33]; b39 on [b33, b38].
Step 7: a Pearl Gold cheese slope (b40) goes on the top stud of the wedge b39. Step 8: the callout sub-assembly (b42 slope on towball plate b41) clips onto the front towball of b38 via b41's socket.

The slope in the callout looks dark gray with a top stud. I read it as lego-92946 (dark gray, 4 in the parts list). The matching piece on page 8 (b30) was recorded as lego-3049d black, which was probably a misread. It is likely lego-92946 as well.
Another orange slope is already visible on this leg in step 7, which I did not see added on page 11. I did not add it here.
rests_on: b40 on [b39]; b41 on []; b42 on [b41].
Step 10 adds no new pieces. The second leg is joined to the underside of the body, beside the first leg.

I couldn't see the exact join point. As on page 9, I recorded the leg's top stud (b42's stud) going into the underside of the round plate b1, at a different position from the first leg. This is a guess.
Two orange slopes are visible on the first leg and one on the front of each foot in the picture. I could not match these to pieces that were not already recorded, so I added none.

I added the pieces the parts list says are missing: 2x 14418, 4x 54200 (1 Pearl Gold, 3 Light Bluish Gray) and 2x 92946. The picture quality is too low to be sure where they go, so their positions are best guesses. The 14418 sockets are read as toe caps on the ball of each foot plate (b29, b41). The cheese slopes are put on those toe caps. The 92946 slopes are put on the leg wedges.

Two earlier pieces probably have the wrong type, and I can't change them because only additions are allowed. b2 (page 2, the plate under the body) was recorded as lego-3020 but is the light gray 2x3 plate lego-3021. b12 (page 4, a black slope on the body) was recorded as lego-60481 but is probably a lego-92946. Fixing these gives the right counts: three 3020 would become two, and 3021 would be three. That is why I did not add a third 3021 or a third 92946.
So the checker will still show lego-3020 +1, lego-3021 -1, lego-60481 +1 and lego-92946 -1 until b2 and b12 are retyped. These are my mistakes, not separate models in the booklet.
This is a single model, so the pieces from the build all belong to one graph.

The four remaining mismatches come from two earlier pieces recorded with the wrong type, not from missing pieces. b2 (page 2) should be lego-3021, not lego-3020. b12 (page 4) should be lego-92946, not lego-60481.

I have not added a 3021 or a 92946 to cancel the 'missing' lines, because that would put pieces in the graph that the booklet never builds and would push those types over the parts list. Since only additions are allowed, I can't retype b2 and b12. Retyping them is the correct fix and would bring every count into line with the parts list.
After that retyping, the pieces match the list: 3020 x2 (b21, b32), 3021 x3 (b2, b22, b33), 60481 x4 (b25, b26, b36, b37) and 92946 x4 (b12, b42, b49, b50).
